title: Credit damage despite loyalty and clean history
content: I have been a loyal Toyota Finance customer for over 6 years with a perfect payment history — not a single missed or late payment. Unfortunately, my recent experience has been deeply disappointing and financially damaging.Due to a claim placed by Toyota Insurance (not by me), I was forced to return my vehicle. I did not initiate this claim, yet it impacted my insurance policy, and as a result, I returned the vehicle under a voluntary agreement. Despite this, Toyota Finance reported my account as delinquent to credit agencies — even after offering me a payment arrangement for the remaining balance.This is unfair and potentially unlawful under several consumer protection standards, including:🔹 The Consumer Credit Act 1974 (UK) / Fair Credit Reporting Act (FCRA – USA): These laws require accurate and fair reporting of consumer credit behavior. Reporting a delinquency while simultaneously offering a payment plan and knowing the customer has not defaulted in good faith may constitute unfair or inaccurate reporting.🔹 The Principles of Treating Customers Fairly (FCA – UK): Lenders must act in the best interest of the customer and treat them with fairness, particularly those in vulnerable or unexpected situations.As a result of this negative mark on my credit file, I have been declined finance by another vehicle dealer, even though the situation was not due to financial irresponsibility but rather an insurance-related technicality entirely out of my control. This damage is not only unjust — it is long-lasting.I am extremely disappointed that Toyota Finance, despite my long-standing, spotless history, chose to report my account in a way that severely impacts my ability to access credit. I am now pursuing options to escalate this through:A formal complaint to Toyota FinanceRaising a dispute with the credit reference agenciesSubmitting a complaint to the Financial Ombudsman Service (UK) or the Consumer Financial Protection Bureau (USA)Seeking legal advice for defamation of creditLoyal customers deserve better — especially those who have upheld every part of their agreement. I urge Toyota Finance to reconsider their reporting decision and correct this unjust entry on my credit file.

title: Lease Buyout Nightmare
content: I have leased vehicles through Toyota/Lexus Financial Services for many decades, with no issues. They even gave me lease extensions during the COVID years, when I was reluctant to go car shopping--or anywhere!But I am writing about my current experience.My lease is up at the end of this month. I decided to buy the car, since leasing a new vehicle (same model, different year) would have cost nearly twice what I am currently paying--BEFORE the tariffs that are making America great and certain corporations and individuals wealthier--go into effect.  So I phoned Toyota Financial to get the buyout information and documents.First of all, the company is technologically in the dark ages. Maybe even prehistoric.Although they were able (at my insistence) to send me he paperwork I needed via email, I had to print, complete, and return the documents to them (by mail) along with a paper check for the buyout amount plus sales tax. They even sent me a form for California residents, though I live 3,000 miles from California.They are incapable or doing electronic bank transfers, accepting credit cards, etc. Just paper checks. (Fortunately, I still have a checkbook, but the last time I used it was 2007.)So, I did what I was supposed to do, and sent the documents and check to Toyota via Priority Mail.  Tracking indicated that it was delivered on 3/26.Eight days later, my bank records showed that the check still had not been cashed. I phoned the company, went through their annoying telephone menu, and after about 10 minutes, I got a "human" (and I use that word loosely) on the line. He was an arrogant and extremely unhelpful young man, whose only response to my inquiry about why my check had not been deposited was, "It takes 10 days for processing," and it was only day 8.  I imagine that for them, processing means opening the mail, then sending an employee to the bank to make deposits, since they are incapable of conducting business electronically.The rep could not or would not tell me how long it would take, once my documents were "processed, "for the bill of sale and title to be sent to me.And how would it be sent? By US mail, of course, which lately, in my experience, has been taking up to a full month for cards and letters to be delivered. They would not send my documents by Priority Mail. My only alternative was to pay an exorbitant fee for FedEx overnight service.It is now 4/5 or 11 days since Toyota received my check, and it still has not been deposited.To compound the absurd wait, Toyota will not transfer the existing vehicle registration to me, which means that I have to go to DMV and wait for hours to register the car in my name.  But wait....They have no way to inform me when the documents I need to register the car have been "processed" and mailed. The current registration, in the name of Toyota, is due in 3 weeks. In all likelihood, I will have to pay to renew the existing Toyota registration, then go to DMV and pay AGAIN to obtain new registration in my name.This is possibly the WORST customer service I have ever received in my life.I asked the arrogant customer disservice representative if he enjoyed working for a company that made things as difficult as possible for their clients, and he merely repeated that "processing takes 10 days."One more thing. I had been told a while ago that I could do the buyout through the dealership from which I had leased it. I thought that would simplify things and had intended to do that. However, when I met with someone at the dealership, I was informed that I would have to pay $900 in fees and various service charges for them to do the transaction--plus title and registration fees to the State. And they also would accept only cash or a paper check. Thanks, but no thanks.All I can say is, that if I ever want to lease a Toyota/Lexus vehicle again, it will be through a bank, NOT Toyota Financial Disservices.

title: Toyota Financial Services Mafia
content: I attempted to pay off my car loan with Toyota Financial Services (TFS) on August 13, 2024, by sending in a check. However, at the beginning of September, I received a notification that I was behind on a loan payment. Concerned, I contacted Toyota Financial to inquire about the situation. During my call, a representative from TFS informed me that they had not received my check and that I needed to make a payment to avoid late fees.Initially, Toyota had informed me that they received the check, had processed my loan to a zero balance, and had released the lien on the title. However, about 30-40 days later (around September 23), after the check had been sent, they reestablished the loan and indicated that the payoff was not processed as originally agreed. Following this, I cancelled the check.M&T Bank has documented evidence showing that the payment was made. It appears that there was internal miscommunication at Toyota Financial, as one department reported receiving the payment while another did not. I have made multiple attempts to reach out to Toyota's customer service through my loan account, but their response was dismissive, only stating that I was behind on my payments. They provided no further assistance or clarification.After this incident, I received the free and clear title to the car about two weeks later, but despite this, I continued to face issues when trying to resolve the situation. I called Toyota multiple times, trying to pay off the loan for the original amount I had sent in August, minus the most recent payments. However, Toyota informed me that the payoff amount had increased and they would need to seek approval to potentially forgive the additional interest. This response was unacceptable to me, as there was no guarantee they would do so, and I felt Toyota was mishandling the situation. Their actions were damaging my credit, and I lost confidence in Toyota Financial Services' ability to resolve the issue fairly and competently.On December 13, I attempted to reach out again, but once again, I was met with unreasonable responses. TFS insisted that I allow the check to go through their process, which could take several months. I believe this is an unfair and unreasonable delay—especially given that any legitimate car loan service should be able to process a payoff within 30 days. It feels like I am being extorted for the additional interest by Toyota Financial Services, which is unacceptable.I have continued to make payments in September, October, November, and December, but I am still accruing interest, which is frustrating and unjust considering the error was on Toyota's part. Therefore, I am requesting that Toyota allow me to pay off the loan for the amount I initially attempted to pay in August and waive any interest that has accrued since then due to their mistake.If Toyota Financial Services continues to make things difficult, I will consider taking further action to regain ownership of the car without additional payments. I am questioning their legal claim to the loan or the vehicle, especially since they released the title to me. At this point, their behavior is more reminiscent of a coercive organization, not a legitimate financial service. They are preventing me from paying off my loan, damaging my credit, and jeopardizing my job due to my security clearance.I am seeking assistance from the Consumer Financial Protection Bureau (CFPB) to help resolve this matter and to investigate how many other individuals Toyota Financial Services may be mistreating with either their incompetence or what feels like extortion.

title: Think carefully
content: Hi all,I took out an agreement with Toyota Finance in 2021. I love the car! I am certain I was told that I could pay off any sums I wanted after a set period and this would affect the final amount I owed. I recently tried to do this to discover this is not the case. The end sum stays the same even if you pay money in the interim. All paying early does is shorten the agreement or decrease the monthly payments.For older people, this kind of agreement does not work. So I would recommend anyone over 55 thinks carefully about taking out an agreement with these people.

title: Toyota Financial doesn't release titles
content: If you ask the rep at Toyota financial, they will tell you that it is their policy to release titles after a lien is paid off. Our family has owned a lot of Toyotas and I can say that has never happened once. You have to contact Toyota Financial and that is process is always awful. You can have them call you back rather than wait on hold but what I got out of that was a call from the company robot with no one on the other end, just silence. You can call back and stay on hold and listen to an awful twangy bit of country pop that repeats several times a minute and will burn itself into your brain. Finally talk to a human and he will tell you whatever he feels is right, you follow the steps and wait for the doc to arrive and after several weeks you call back and after ten minutes of more of that awful song designed to make you hang up, you get informed that you were misinformed and you need to fax different docs, which no one felt any obligation to inform you of until you personally go through the aggravation of calling back. Even worse, they insist of having the docs arrive by fax. Anyone still have a working fax machine? It will cost me about $40 to fax the docs that they didn't know they wanted until they rejected what they first asked for. My case was closed until I called back. What do we make of a company that markets itself for its advanced tech and hasn't figured out email by 2022? We've had to deal with this four times in the last 3 years. It's enough to make me think twice about ever signing up for this treatment by buying Toyota ever again.

title: Due to covid 19 pandemic my work hours…
content: Due to covid 19 pandemic my work hours were cut as well as my fiancé loosing her job and the arrival of our newborn son has gotten really tight. Toyota deferred a few payments and things slowly went back to normal and I have never been late or missed a payment since. I asked again for the same courtesy after the truck had grave mechanical issues just hitting the 100k mark. Now with the covid resurgence and no longer being paid for the days we miss, money has got tight. I was denied, I have spoken with multiple friends in the same predicament and have been given courtesy by other lenders. I feel Toyota does not stand by it’s products and does not care about its customers, only the paycheck. My families Christmas was shot this year and just trying to pay my bills is getting tough. My company a large commercial mechanical contractor in NJ will discontinue use of Toyota Tundra vehicles and be going with Ford now. I am a combat veteran and hard working American and this will be my last Toyota vehicle. I just want others to know about Toyota financials incompassion and warn you before you spend 60k on their product like I did.
